motion.value: 30% of card width, or flick > 0.5px/ms over >= 30px within 100ms

motion.name: resist
motion.purpose: Give when there is no neighbor in that direction.

motion.value: cross-document view transition, names field-help / field-ask, 460ms var(--ease-out); group overflow clip, z-index 1, 18px radius from 960px; group background in the field color only under types keep-help / keep-ask (both pages carry the field), otherwise the partnerless field just fades; snapshots object-fit none, object-position left bottom

motion.name: how-cut
motion.value: clip-path inset(0 0 0 100%) + translateX(32px) to rest, 420ms var(--ease-out); old step fades and moves 32px left, 220ms ease-in
motion.purpose: Each story step's content (how-step) wipes in from the right.

motion.name: how-back
motion.value: view transition type back: clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) + translateX(-32px) in, old leaves 32px right
motion.purpose: Going back a step, to the doors (step 0), or from sign-up (step 99) to the story reverses the cut; set by how.js on pagereveal.

motion.name: how-open
motion.value: view transition type open: incoming how-step delayed 220ms
motion.purpose: Opening a door or switching stories lets the field land before the words cut in.

motion.name: join-handoff
motion.value: view transition name join-card on .how-end / .join-card, 460ms var(--ease-out), group overflow clip at var(--radius), z-index 2 with how-step; old snapshot centered, fades out 120ms after 100ms ease-in; new snapshot left top, fades in 200ms ease-out
motion.purpose: The last step's green Sign up grows into the sign-up form card while the step words cut and the field sinks into the strip; reduced motion is plain navigation.

motion.name: how-swipe
motion.purpose: Swipe or arrow keys follow the Back / Next links on story steps.

narrative.overview:
The app is a tip jar on a counter: small gifts from passersby, dropped in one at a time. The ground is pale jar glass (bg), the shell (top bar, phone nav, theme color, app icon) is a soft dollar green with white type, and inside it a single ask fills the screen as a light green field, Want Sage for helping and Need Seafoam for asking, with its title set huge in condensed uppercase in dark green ink. You move through people sideways: drag left for the next ask, drag right to go back, and the neighboring ask's field is already waiting underneath, so every move reads as a cut from one field to the next rather than a scroll. The one money action, Chip in, is a marigold tab, the jar's masking-tape label and the one warm note in the world, so giving never blends into the green chrome. There is no black anywhere: the darkest value is a green-black ink (#16261d).

The world is always light. There is no dark mode, and `prefers-color-scheme` is ignored (`color-scheme: light`). The working pages (Gifts, Leaders, profile, forms, admin, legal) are quiet and dense on the same ground with white panels, the same two typefaces, the same green filled button, and the same hairline language. Lists are hairline rows, progress is a single hairline meter, and states are a small shape plus a word. There are no shadows, glass, or glow, and no dark scrim. The only gradients are fades into the field's own color: photos dissolve into the solid field so the words always sit on field.

The system is built for a phone held in one hand. It works at 360px without horizontal scroll and works without JavaScript, because every gesture has a real link behind it. At 960px and wider, the nav moves up into the bar, and the feed card takes the post page's shape: a wide landscape ask joined to a 400px Chip in panel, with big Back and Next buttons outside it. On a monitor nobody has to drag.
keyCharacteristics: A pale jar-glass ground and a soft dollar-green shell with white type. Always light, no black anywhere.
One full-bleed light green field per ask (Want Sage or Need Seafoam) with dark green ink and no scrim.
League Gothic uppercase for titles, set huge and tall. Public Sans for everything else.
A green filled primary, outlined secondary, a marigold Chip in as the one warm note, and tomato only for errors and destructive acts.
Hairline meter, hairline rows, and Lucide 2px line icons.
Sideways gestures with a way back: left = next, right = back, each mirrored by a labeled rail button.

rules.name: The Dark Ink On Field Rule
rules.body: On a Sage or Seafoam field, every word and glyph is green-black ink (on-field, or on-field-muted for secondary lines), never white and never under a scrim. Filled controls on a field are only Marigold (Chip in), Dollar Green (the primary, such as the last step's Sign up), Press Green (a lit rail glyph), or a white example panel.

rules.name: The One Warm Note Rule
rules.body: Marigold is Chip in and nothing else: the feed card's tab and its example on the How stories. It never becomes a category, a badge, or decoration.

rules.name: The No Black Rule
rules.body: No black and no neutral gray-black anywhere. The darkest color is the green-black ink (#16261d). (The `#000` inside a mask-image gradient is an alpha stop, not a rendered color.)

rules.name: The Always Light Rule
rules.body: There is no dark mode. The root declares `color-scheme: light`, and nothing reads `prefers-color-scheme`.

rules.name: The Tomato Is Trouble Rule
rules.body: The bad family appears only for errors, disputed gifts, and destructive actions. It is never decoration, never a category, and never the Chip in color.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: League Gothic is only for titles and the wordmark, always uppercase. Every sentence, label, number, and control is Public Sans. Don't use a system face for display.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every amount, count, rank, and badge number uses tabular numerals.

rules.name: The Field Fade Only Rule
rules.body: The only gradients are fades into the field's own color. The feed card photo is masked transparent at 4%, solid from 18 to 30%, and transparent by 58%, and a photo card washes the field (85% field to transparent by 22%) behind the tabs. The post-hero photo is masked solid to 30% and transparent by 62%. The door and step mosaics fade to solid field before the words. Never a dark scrim, a fade to another hue, glass, glow, or a box or drop shadow.

dos: **Do** keep the top bar and phone nav Dollar Green (#3a7558) with white type, the pages on the jar-glass ground, and the whole app light whatever the system setting.
**Do** give each ask a full-bleed Sage or Seafoam field with field-ink type and no scrim, and check that any new category color holds dark ink at 4.5:1 or better.
**Do** fade every photo into the field's own color so the words, tabs, and Chip in sit on solid field.
**Do** set titles in League Gothic uppercase and everything else in Public Sans, with tabular numerals for money and counts.
**Do** use the green filled button for the screen's main action, Marigold only for Chip in, and outline everything else.
**Do** show progress only with the hairline meter, and lists only as hairline rows.
**Do** use Lucide line icons at a 2px stroke from the `_icons.html` sprite, always with a visible text label.
**Do** back every gesture with a labeled button and a real link, so the feed works without JavaScript and at 360px with no horizontal scroll.
**Do** say "gift" and "chip in" in interface copy.
**Do** label every demo piece of the app "Example" with the outlined tag, and make it mirror the real component and its real state exactly.
donts: **Don't** use black or a neutral gray-black anywhere, or add a dark mode.
**Don't** put white text or a dark scrim on a Sage or Seafoam field.
**Don't** use Marigold for anything but Chip in, or tomato for anything but errors, disputed gifts, and destructive actions.
**Don't** add box or drop shadows, glass, glow, or gradients other than the fades into the field's own color.
**Don't** turn state into pills or badges with fills. Use a shape and a word.

**Don't** add a second progress style for money or goals (rings, segmented bars, or percentages as hero numbers). The segmented step bars on the How stories mark place in a story, never progress toward a goal.
**Don't** nest cards in panels or lay asks out as a card grid or vertical-scroll feed.
**Don't** say "donation" or "charity" anywhere in the interface.
**Don't** invent stats, counts, testimonials, or quotes on marketing surfaces. The proof is the real app pieces, labeled Example.
